subject: hoverPickup
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: militarized pickup converted to hover thrusters.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static hover pickup model without joints, keeping the builder geometry simple and sticking to safe, well-supported methods like part, extrude, and lathe rather than riskier API calls.

I'm sizing the vehicle to roughly 5.4m long, 2.1m wide, 1.9m tall, with hover thrusters and small landing skids touching the ground to give the parked vehicle visual stability. Now I'm working out the chassis box dimensions and extruding the cab and body silhouette along the side profile, calculating the cross products to get the extrusion direction right while sketching the rear-to-front outline points.

Still shaping the body geometry...

Still working out the hood and body silhouette extrusion profile...

Now I'm designing the hover thrusters as corner nacelles with cylindrical ducts, glowing discs, and landing pod geometry positioned at each corner near the floor.

Checking the pod widths against a real pickup's dimensions, stylized is fine. I'm adjusting the pod cylinder to sit flush near y=0 so the lowest points nearly touch the ground without z-fighting against the glow disc.

Now I'm adding extras: a roof turret with cylindrical barrels and shield plate, light bar, antenna, armor panels, bull bar, neon magenta headlight and underglow strips, bed rollbar, ammo boxes, cyberpunk dark paint with neon stripe decals, and skull/hazard emblem textures on the doors.

Adding more textures and paint helpers...

Now I'm sketching the hover truck's part list—chassis, underbelly plate, hood—working out box dimensions and positions for each piece.

Continuing the part layout...

Adjusting the cab base profile so it sits properly on the chassis over the hood, tweaking the polygon points to keep it convex and the bottom edge aligned at y=0.79 across the chassis width.

Now I'm planning the roof armor plate and light bar, then adding door details like side windows, emblem decals, and a hazard stripe panel, with the glass textured dark teal with glowing cyan streaks for both windshield and side windows.

Designing the turret next: a base cylinder with a ring and pivot post, a boxy gun body, twin cylindrical barrels extending forward, a shield plate positioned just ahead of the body, glowing muzzle tips, and a side ammo box. Then I'll move on to placing the thrusters at each corner position.

For the thrusters, I'm working out each pod as a tapered cylinder with a darker accent ring near the top, an upward-facing intake fan disc, a glowing cyan exhaust disc at the bottom, and a strut box connecting the pod to the body.

Checking the neon ring radius against the cylinder's taper so it sits flush against the pod surface, then sketching side skirt armor plates and underglow strips between the pods.

Now I'm adding smaller details: roof sensor dome, spotlight, rear tail lights glowing red-magenta, and rear hover thrusters with glow discs. I'm also planning a decal emblem plane on the bed sides.

That reasoning holds for the right side too, so I'll trust the plane orientation logic for windows as well. Now I'm sketching out the SVG textures: a glass panel with dark gradient and cyan diagonal streaks plus a HUD line, a fan with radial blades and a hub, yellow-black hazard stripes, and a neon bed tag reading "HV-07" with a skull glyph.

I'm adding a hood decal with a magenta chevron, oriented with the up vector pointing toward +z so it faces front correctly, and designing an underglow disc with radial cyan rings plus a thruster nozzle texture of concentric cyan rings separated by dark gaps.

Now I'm sketching helper functions for building box-shaped parts with color and placement options, confirming that a model with no joints can still work since static models can omit joints entirely, and setting up mirrored pairs using a simple [1,-1] loop while figuring out how to apply paint color correctly to the hull's box geometry.

Thinking about nested paint functions for camo stripes on the hood and roof, plus antennas and rods placed without joints. Adding a sensor dome on the roof using a partial sphere, a glowing spotlight bar, and considering rocket pods mounted on the bed-side shoulders.

Positioning additional rocket pods on the cab roof sides with small dark cylindrical tubes, then finalizing the export while double-checking the barrel and circle orientation parameters so cylinders aim correctly along their axes.
